data.title: Multidrug therapy (MDT) for leprosy
data.summary: Antileprosy drugs · NLEP 3-drug multidrug therapy (rifampicin + clofazimine + dapsone) for both PB and MB leprosy — revised regimen in force from 1 April 2025
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antileprosy drugs_

**Class:** NLEP 3-drug multidrug therapy (rifampicin + clofazimine + dapsone) for both PB and MB leprosy — revised regimen in force from 1 April 2025

## Mechanism of action
- Combining a bactericidal drug (rifampicin) with bacteriostatic drugs (dapsone, clofazimine) prevents resistance and kills persisters
- Monthly supervised doses ensure the key drug (rifampicin) is taken
- Since 1 April 2025 India uses the same three drugs for PB and MB (WHO 2018 recommendation); only the duration differs

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Revised NLEP classification:
- Paucibacillary (PB): 1–5 skin lesions AND no nerve involvement AND slit-skin smear negative
- Multibacillary (MB): more than 5 skin lesions, OR involvement of one or more nerves, OR slit-skin smear positive
- (Change from the old classification: any nerve involvement now makes the case MB)
- Adult (PB and MB): rifampicin 600 mg once monthly (supervised) + clofazimine 300 mg once monthly (supervised) + clofazimine 50 mg daily + dapsone 100 mg daily
- Duration: PB 6 months; MB 12 months
- Child 10–14 years (PB 6 months / MB 12 months): rifampicin 450 mg monthly + clofazimine 150 mg monthly + clofazimine 50 mg on alternate days + dapsone 50 mg daily
- Child under 10 years (or 20–40 kg): rifampicin 10 mg/kg monthly + clofazimine 100 mg monthly + clofazimine 50 mg twice weekly + dapsone 2 mg/kg daily; separate single-drug formulations are used under 40 kg where packs are not suitable
- Patients already on treatment on 31 March 2025 complete their old regimen (PB 2-drug MDT; MB MDT) until release from treatment
- Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP): single-dose rifampicin (SDR-PEP) to eligible contacts of an index case (NLEP, since 2017)
- Rifampicin-resistant leprosy (WHO 2018): clofazimine + two of ofloxacin/moxifloxacin, minocycline, clarithromycin
- Terms from Khopkar often asked in viva: U-MDT (uniform MDT trial — one regimen for all), A-MDT (accompanied MDT — full course handed over at diagnosis), ROM (rifampicin 600 mg + ofloxacin 400 mg + minocycline 100 mg)

## Dose & formulations
- Blister packs: adult and child packs supplied free under NLEP (WHO supply of revised packs from April 2025)
- Instructions to patients: take the monthly dose in front of the health worker; urine may turn red; skin darkens with clofazimine and fades after treatment; report reactions, nerve pain or weakness at once; treatment is free

## Adverse effects
- See individual drugs
- Leprosy reactions may occur during or after treatment and are treated without stopping MDT: type 1 (reversal) — prednisolone 40 mg/day tapered over about 12–20 weeks; type 2 (ENL) — prednisolone, thalidomide, clofazimine

## Contraindications
- Rifampicin hypersensitivity/resistance → clofazimine-based alternative regimens
- Dapsone allergy → omit dapsone, continue rifampicin + clofazimine

## Monitoring
- Monthly review: compliance, reactions, nerve function (voluntary muscle testing and sensory testing), drug side effects
- Notification is mandatory from all sectors (government, private, NGO, medical colleges) — Nikusth portal
- Release from treatment after the fixed duration; follow up for relapse and reactions

## Pregnancy & lactation
MDT is safe and should be continued in pregnancy and breastfeeding; reactions may flare after delivery.

## Viva points
- Revised classification (2025): any nerve involvement = MB
- 3 drugs for both PB (6 months) and MB (12 months) since 1 April 2025
- Adult and child doses — clofazimine 50 mg daily (adult), alternate days (10–14 y), twice weekly (<10 y)
- SDR-PEP for contacts; leprosy is notifiable from all sectors

## Note on sources
Updated to the NLEP regimen in force from 1 April 2025 (MoHFW/DGHS NLEP page and DO letter). The older 2-drug PB regimen is no longer used for new patients.

_Sources: NLEP / MoHFW revised classification and treatment regimen (DGHS letter Z-14020/80/2023-Lep, 17 Jan 2024; implemented from 1 Apr 2025, DO letter 6 Mar 2025); WHO Guidelines for leprosy 2018; Khopkar ch.6 (U-MDT, A-MDT, ROM). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
